clue.text: Dull? Chops one that may follow our speaker

definitions.text: one that may follow our speaker

parts.note: matt describes a surface without shine, so it means dull
to hew is to chop, so chops gives hews

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a dull person chops something that tails a talker.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle's 'speaker' is Stanley, who said the famous line at 9. Sir Stanley Matthews was a celebrated English footballer, so his surname follows the word Stanley.
explanation.definitionFit: The footballer Sir Stanley Matthews has a surname that comes straight after the explorer's name Stanley.

clue.text: Look round very fast

indicators.note: round says the look word goes around the abbreviation for very

parts.note: to stare is to look hard

explanation.surface: An instruction to glance about quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' reads as an adverb meaning quickly, but it is the verb meaning go without food.
explanation.definitionFit: To fast is to go without food, and to starve is to go without it too.

clue.text: Exaggerated heading off little rodent: write this up in book

indicators.note: in a down entry writing something up means entering it from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means exaggerated

indicators.note: heading off says the first letter of the rodent's name is dropped

parts.note: a gerbil is a small rodent kept as a pet

explanation.surface: An overblown headline about a tiny rodent, to be written up in a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' drops the G of GERBIL, leaving ERBIL; OTT plus ERBIL makes OTTERBIL, and 'write this up' turns it to read upwards in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The words of an opera or musical are its book, the text the composer sets.

clue.text: No more hesitation lifting this from seabed

indicators.note: lifting in a down entry makes the letters rise, so they read upwards in reverse

parts.note: less can mean no more, as in no more than
um is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A diver stops dithering and hauls something up from the sea floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifting' turns LESSUM, so it reads upwards in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A mussel is a shellfish that lives on rocks and the sea floor, and it gets brought up from there.

clue.text: 9, for example, with no points to make a book

indicators.note: points are compass points, and the two compass letters in the shape word are removed

parts.note: nine is a square number, three times three
taken as written

explanation.surface: Nine, used as an example with no decimal points, somehow makes up a volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no points' removes the compass points S and E from SQUARE, leaving QUAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarto is a book size made by folding each printing sheet twice into four leaves.

clue.text: Enough people after status — weird

parts.note: in the Latin phrase status quo the word quo comes after status
rum is an old-fashioned word for odd or weird

explanation.surface: A grumble that people chasing status are a strange lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' meaning odd is old-fashioned British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A quorum is the minimum number of members needed for a meeting to make valid decisions.

clue.text: Drink is sweet, with no ice

indicators.note: with no tells us the word ice is taken away from the sweet

parts.note: liquorice is a black chewy sweet flavoured with the root of the liquorice plant

explanation.surface: A drink described as sweet and served without ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweet' looks like it describes the drink, but it is a noun, the confectionery.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquor is alcoholic drink, especially spirits.

clue.text: Notice about 1 follower

parts.note: re means about or concerning
1 is Matthew, and Mark's gospel follows Matthew's in the New Testament

explanation.surface: A notice about someone who follows another.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1 refers to the answer at 1, read as the gospel writer Matthew.
explanation.definitionFit: To remark something is to notice or observe it, as is a remark itself.

clue.text: See 9
Falsify income: small forged note and small coin to pick up — there you are!

parts.note: to doctor accounts is to falsify them
a living is what one earns, an income

indicators.note: forged here means faked or reworked, so the letters of note are rearranged

parts.note: 1p, a penny, is a small coin, read as I and P
to resume is to pick up where one left off

explanation.surface: A fraudster cooks the books, forges a note and pockets loose change, then says here it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forged' rearranges NOTE into TONE. The small coin is 1p, the penny, written as IP. Henry Morton Stanley greeted the explorer this way on finding him in Africa in 1871.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous greeting on finding someone long sought is a jokey way of saying here you are at last.

clue.text: See 9
9, follower of some 1 and 7

definitions.meaning: the first answer here is the doctor
the third gospel comes after those of Matthew and Mark in the New Testament

explanation.surface: A doctor who follows two others.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Luke is called the beloved physician, and his gospel comes after Matthew's and Mark's.

clue.text: Tired wife out, keeping arm in correspondence

indicators.note: keeping says the remaining letters hold the weapon inside them
out says the abbreviation for wife leaves the tired word

parts.note: weary means tired
a pistol is a firearm, an arm

explanation.surface: An exhausted wife has gone out, keeping a weapon handy while writing letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arm' is a weapon, not a limb. 'out' and 'keeping' both work on the tired word: first the wife leaves it, then what is left wraps around the gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Epistolary describes something carried on or written in the form of letters.

clue.text: Applying to be computerised is certain to be penalised

parts.note: applying for something is ...
IT is information technology, so for IT means destined for computers

explanation.surface: Applying to have your work computerised is bound to get you punished.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone said to be begging for trouble is behaving so as to invite punishment, an idiom.

clue.text: Untaught foreign lady heading off to place of 11

indicators.note: heading off says the first letter of the lady's title is dropped

parts.note: signora is Italian for a married lady
Luke's gospel is in the New Testament, abbreviated NT

explanation.surface: An untaught Italian woman sets off for the place where a doctor works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' drops the S of SIGNORA, leaving IGNORA.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lacking schooling or knowledge is uneducated, without learning.

clue.text: Commanding size, bigger than 5 across

definitions.meaning: commanding as in majestic or lordly, like an emperor
a traditional paper size larger than quarto

explanation.surface: A grand, commanding size, larger than a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Imperial means majestic and authoritative, and it is also a large sheet size for paper.

clue.text: Terrible fist's second stroke

parts.note: the crawl is a swimming stroke

explanation.surface: A dreadful punch followed by a second blow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fist' is an old word for handwriting, not a clenched hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrawl is untidy, hard-to-read writing, so a bad hand.

clue.text: Grow unpopular and fold

indicators.note: unpopular means not in, so the letters of in are taken away

parts.note: to increase is to grow

explanation.surface: Something becomes disliked and then gives way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fold' looks like the verb meaning collapse, as a failing business does; it is the noun, a crease in paper or cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A fold in fabric or paper leaves a line, the same as a crease.

clue.text: According to short burst on phone, our speaker may be on the other end

definitions.text: our speaker may be on the other end

parts.note: acc is a short form of according

indicators.note: short says the final letter of the phone sound is cut off

parts.note: a ringtone is the burst of sound a mobile makes when called

explanation.surface: Going by a quick ring, the person speaking might be at the far end of the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops the last E of RINGTONE. Accrington Stanley is an English football club, so Stanley comes at the other end of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lancashire town's football club is called Accrington Stanley, putting the explorer's name at its end.

clue.text: Corrected in ballpoint?

parts.note: a red pen is the corrector's ballpoint, so work fixed with one could be called done again

explanation.surface: A question whether something was fixed using a biro.
explanation.walkthrough: Split differently, the answer is RED ONE, the red ballpoint teachers mark with.
explanation.definitionFit: Work that has been corrected has been done over, carried out a second time.

clue.text: Dead queen 9, for example

parts.note: a dead limb is numb, without feeling
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual abbreviation for the queen

explanation.surface: A late queen held up as one instance of a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: '9' looks like a pointer to the doctor at 9, but here it is simply the figure nine.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine is an example of a numeral or figure.

clue.text: Drink, one put before our speaker

definitions.meaning: ... Stanley is the capital of the Falkland Islands, so the word goes before Stanley

explanation.surface: A drink, with one poured for the person giving a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Port is a sweet fortified wine, and Port Stanley is a town whose name starts with it.

clue.text: Damn! Rain spoiled the fruit

indicators.note: spoiled suggests something ruined and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone curses because rain has ruined the harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandarin is a small citrus fruit like a tangerine.

clue.text: Mass disseminator of News Corporation, if our speaker joined

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for mass in physics
an organ is a newspaper or journal that spreads news

explanation.surface: A huge spreader of news at Murdoch's company, should the speaker sign up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'News Corporation' looks like Murdoch's media group, but it splits across two jobs. Morgan Stanley is a large American investment bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Add the explorer's name and you get the big financial corporation Morgan Stanley.

clue.text: Plan in atmosphere to hold weather-changing event

indicators.note: to hold says the words plan in atmosphere contain the answer within them

explanation.surface: A scheme to keep something in the air that will change the weather.
explanation.definitionFit: La Nina is a cooling of the Pacific Ocean that shifts weather patterns around the world.

clue.text: Stick around, breaking compiler's threat

indicators.note: breaking says the stick word splits the setter's pronoun apart

parts.note: the compiler is the setter, who refers to themself as me

indicators.note: around says the stick word is turned the other way

parts.note: a cane is a stick

explanation.surface: A setter waves a stick about in a threatening way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' looks like it describes the stick snapping, but it is the signal that the setter's pronoun is split open; 'around' means the stick is turned backwards before it goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: A menace is a danger or threat.
